name: Main World Planet Size (Step 1)
description: p.91. Step 1: roll 2D-2. Optional: to increase chances of Earth-sized planets, roll 2D+1 instead. Planets larger than 16,000km: roll 2D+3. Moons: roll D3-1 per moon. Results of 1 or less are typically manufactured locations such as orbital space colonies, mining asteroids, or other orbital modules like bases, starports made of manufactured materials, hollowed asteroids, or a combination of both. These locations require a full artificial environment for habitation. Gravity is grouped in the book: 0 Minimal to none; 1-3 0.25G; 4-6 0.5G; 7-9 1G; 10-11 1.5G; 12 2G. BOOK: the size table on p.91 prints 17,700km and 19,3000km; this table uses 17,600km and 19,200km from the chart on p.90 (steps of 1,600km).

name: Main World Government (Step 5)
description:
Roll with the Toolkit's world generator, or add the DMs below by hand: add the population code. A direct draw from this table uses no DMs and gives the wrong spread.

p.92. Step 5: roll 2D-7 and add the population code to determine the average governing system found on the world.

results.text: Gov: 0 · Type: None · Description: No formal governing structure except for family and interpersonal relationships.

Gov: 1 · Type: Company/Corporation · Description: For-profit organizations run by managerial elites who govern the citizenry with corporate organizational structures. Corpo-feudal, private-sponsored colonies, etc.
Gov: 2 · Type: Participating Democracy · Description: The citizens have a direct voice in the ruling functions of government via direct democratic methods and assemblies.
Gov: 3 · Type: Self-Perpetuating Oligarchy · Description: The government is led by an elite class who maintains power with minimal to no input from the general population.
Gov: 4 · Type: Representative Democracy · Description: Laws and government are dictated by elected individuals from the general population.
Gov: 5 · Type: Feudal Technocracy · Description: Government functions within a caste-based structure driven by technological implementation.
Gov: 6 · Type: Captive Government · Description: Imposed leader or puppet government controlled by an outside government, to govern the local population.

Gov: 7 · Type: Balkanisation · Description: No central government. Decentralized, small political governments in perpetual conflict and rivalries driven by philosophical, ecological, economical, and social factors. Laws are determined by the local government.

Gov: 8 · Type: Civil Service Bureaucracy · Description: The governing duties are driven by government agencies led by groups and individuals with specific expertise from the general population to maintain civil function and services for everyone.

Gov: 9 · Type: Impersonal Bureaucracy · Description: Governing responsibilities are driven by agencies without input or from the population. Leaders are insulated from the effects of government stagnation.

Gov: 10 (A) · Type: Charismatic Dictator · Description: A single leader determines the rule of law and the direction of society, functioning as a representation of the people they govern, prioritising their culture and influence over others.
Gov: 11 (B) · Type: Non-Charismatic Leader · Description: An impersonal leader who determines the government without popular enthusiasm.
Gov: 12 (C) · Type: Charismatic Oligarchy · Description: The population elevates an elite few to drive society in an ideal direction. The chosen few have the full confidence of the many.
Gov: 13 (D) · Type: Religious Sovereignty · Description: A religious organisation determines the roles of government, driven by spiritual determinants in law and society.
Gov: 14 (E) · Type: Religious Autocracy · Description: A single individual or small group has absolute power over the many via “divine right” and religious authority.

Gov: 15 (F) · Type: Totalitarian Oligarchy · Description: Government is used to force the will of the few onto the many, often with oppressive and coercive methods to maintain and exercise power, to limit the rights of most of the population.

name: Main World Law Level (Step 6)
description:
Roll with the Toolkit's world generator, or add the DMs below by hand: add the government code. A direct draw from this table uses no DMs and gives the wrong spread.

p.93. Step 6: roll 2D-7 and add the government code. Anything banned is also applied to everything listed above it. For example, Law Level 7 bans everything described in Law Level 7 and less. These laws are applied to both citizens and spacers. However, they might not apply to high SOC members of the local society, such as oligarchs, nobles, or other members of high-status minorities on less-equitable planets. * Law Level 10-15 and the Other category are optional and are provided for the referee to give examples for more oppressive legal restrictions.

description:

p.93. Step 7: roll 2D with DMs based on the world's population: Population 8-9: DM +1; Population 10+: DM +2; Population 3-4: DM -1; Population 2 or less: DM -2. Highport is an orbital spaceport that is geo-positioned over the main planetary starport for higher traffic and service.
